name: Yarlam Resort
summary: The most polished hotel in Lachung, set on the slope above the village near the army camp, with valley-facing rooms, room heating, a restaurant and a spa. It is our pick when a couple or family wants real warmth and comfort before the cold Yumthang morning.
body: Yarlam sits in upper Lachung, above the main bazaar, and the terrace looks straight down the Lachung Chu valley towards the village and its monastery. The Mangan district administration lists it as a four-star property, and in a village where most hotels are simple concrete lodges, that difference shows: heated rooms, proper bedding, a restaurant that can manage North Indian, Chinese and continental plates, and staff used to early starts for Yumthang.

Expect to pay several times a budget room, and book well ahead for April–May rhododendron season and the October–November clear-weather weeks. Lachung sits at about 2,700 m, so even here we suggest a slow first evening, plenty of water and no alcohol on night one. Rates and inclusions change by season: check current status before you travel.
why: The warmest, quietest rooms in Lachung after a cold Yumthang day
Terrace views over the valley and the Lachung monastery side
Kitchen used to packing early breakfasts for Zero Point starts

faqs.q: Is Yarlam Resort worth the extra cost in Lachung?
faqs.a: If you feel the cold, are travelling with older parents or want one night of real comfort, yes. Lachung nights drop below zero from December to February and stay cold most of the year. Budget lodges often rely on one blanket and a plug-in heater. Yarlam is warmer, quieter and better run. For hardy travellers on a tight budget, a family homestay at a fifth of the price is fine.

faqs.q: Can we book Yarlam inside a North Sikkim package?
faqs.a: Yes. Most travellers reach Lachung on a 2-night or 3-night North Sikkim package, because permits and vehicles must go through Sikkim Tourism-registered agents. Ask us for a comfort or premium package and we will quote Yarlam with your car, permits and meals. The hotel upgrade usually adds ₹12,000–20,000 per couple over a budget package for two nights, depending on season.

faqs.q: Does Yarlam Resort have heating and hot water?
faqs.a: Guests and listings describe heated rooms, bed warmers and hot water, which is what you are paying for in Lachung. Power cuts do happen across North Sikkim, and the best hotels run generators. Carry a warm layer for the room anyway, and ask at check-in what time hot water is strongest, since early-morning Yumthang starts can coincide with the morning rush.

name: Le Coxy Resort
summary: A larger, modern resort at Fakha on the Lachung side of the valley, popular with families for spacious rooms, heated mattresses and a buffet breakfast. It is a step up from standard package hotels without the price of Yarlam.
body: Le Coxy stands at Fakha (also spelled Faka), the lower part of Lachung where many of the newer hotels have come up along the road. Guest reviews regularly mention clean, roomy rooms, heated mattresses and packed breakfasts for the pre-dawn run to Yumthang and Zero Point, which is the practical test of any Lachung hotel.

Because it is big, Le Coxy is a common upgrade in group and family packages, and it can feel busy on peak weekends in May and October. Ask for an upper-floor, valley-side room. Rates vary sharply between the rhododendron season, the October–November peak and the quiet monsoon. Check current status before you travel.
why: Spacious rooms that suit families of three or four
Heated mattresses, which matter more than décor at 2,700 m
Packed breakfasts for early Yumthang and Zero Point departures

faqs.q: Where is Le Coxy Resort in Lachung?
faqs.a: It is at Fakha, on the road through lower Lachung, a few minutes by car from the bazaar. All Lachung hotels lie along the same valley road, so location matters less than room quality. From Le Coxy it is about 24 km and 1–1.5 hours to Yumthang Valley, and roughly another hour to Zero Point when the road is open.

faqs.q: Is Le Coxy good for families with children?
faqs.a: Yes for children over five, who are allowed in North Sikkim protected areas. Children under five are not permitted, so a Lachung trip is not possible with toddlers. For older children, Le Coxy's larger rooms, heated beds and buffet meals make it easier than small lodges. Pack warm caps, gloves and a thermos for the Yumthang morning.

faqs.q: What does a comfort package with Le Coxy cost?
faqs.a: As an indicative 2026 figure, a 2-night Lachung package from Gangtok with a private SUV, permits, Le Coxy and meals works out around ₹11,000–15,000 per person for two people sharing, more in May and October. The Zero Point drive is extra, usually ₹3,000–4,000 per vehicle. Ask us for a current quote before you book flights.

name: Fortuna Lachung
summary: A well-reviewed mid-range hotel near the police check post on the Yumthang road, with valley views and staff who understand cold-weather guests. Good value for couples and small families who want more than a basic lodge.
body: Fortuna stands near the check post on the road out of Lachung towards Yumthang, which saves a few minutes on the morning drive. Rooms are simple but neat, and guests mention extra blankets on request and mountain views from the upper floors. It is a typical good Lachung mid-range hotel: no frills, warm enough, and meals served at fixed times in a dining hall.

Most package operators use Fortuna on value-tier North Sikkim trips. Do not confuse it with Delight The Fortuna Sapphire Resort, a separate, newer property in Lachung. If your quote says only Fortuna, ask which one. Rates move with season, so check current status before you travel.
why: On the Yumthang side of the village for an early start
Mountain views and extra blankets on request
Fair middle ground between budget lodges and resorts

faqs.q: Is Fortuna Lachung the same as Fortuna Sapphire Resort?
faqs.a: No. Fortuna Lachung is the older hotel near the police check post on the Yumthang road. Delight The Fortuna Sapphire Resort is a different, newer property in Lachung. Both appear in package quotes, often just as Fortuna, so ask your operator which one is booked. We name the exact hotel in every quote we send.

faqs.q: Are meals included at Fortuna in Lachung?
faqs.a: In North Sikkim packages, hotels are usually booked on a meal plan with dinner and breakfast, and often lunch on the arrival day. There are only a few eateries in Lachung, so eating at the hotel is normal. Expect dal, rice, a vegetable, chicken or egg, and noodles or momos. Tell us in advance about vegetarian or Jain needs.

faqs.q: How cold is it at Fortuna Lachung in winter?
faqs.a: From December to February Lachung night temperatures fall to around −5 °C, and snow is likely. Rooms are heated with plug-in heaters and extra blankets rather than central heating. Bring thermal innerwear, a warm cap and socks for sleeping. October–November nights are cold but clear, around 0–5 °C, and more comfortable for most travellers.

name: Snow Lion Mountain Resort
summary: A friendly, modestly priced hotel near the State Bank ATM in Lachung, close to the river, often praised for its hosts and home-style food. A sensible value choice for travellers who care more about warmth and welcome than décor.
body: Snow Lion Mountain Resort lies close to the State Bank of India ATM in Lachung, a short walk from the Lachung Chu, and on a quiet night you hear the river from the rooms. Reviewers keep returning to the same points: polite, helpful hosts, decent internet by Lachung standards, and good food from the kitchen.

Rooms are plain and clean. Ask for an upper floor if you want a mountain view. Being near the ATM is useful because cards are not accepted everywhere in North Sikkim and the machine is sometimes out of cash: carry enough from Gangtok. Prices change by season; check current status before you travel.
why: Hosts often praised by name in reviews
Near the river and the State Bank ATM in Lachung
Fair price for a warm, clean room with good food

faqs.q: Is there an ATM in Lachung?
faqs.a: Yes, the State Bank of India has a branch and ATM in Lachung, close to Snow Lion Mountain Resort. It can run out of cash in peak season or go offline with the network, so carry enough cash from Gangtok for tips, snacks, boots on rent at Yumthang and the Zero Point add-on. UPI works in many shops when the mobile network holds.

faqs.q: Does Snow Lion have Wi-Fi?
faqs.a: Guests report usable internet, which is better than many Lachung lodges. Treat it as a bonus rather than a promise: North Sikkim networks drop in bad weather and during power cuts. BSNL, Jio and Airtel all have some signal in Lachung village, but there is little or none at Yumthang and Zero Point.

faqs.q: Can solo travellers stay at Snow Lion in Lachung?
faqs.a: Yes, but a solo traveller still has to go through a registered agent for permits, so most join a shared North Sikkim tour from Gangtok. On shared tours the hotel is fixed by the operator, so ask in advance whether Snow Lion can be used. Single occupancy is charged close to the full room rate.

name: Lachung family homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Several Lachungpa families take guests in their homes, with dinner and breakfast cooked in the family kitchen. It is the cheapest way to sleep in Lachung and the best way to understand a village run by its own Dzumsa council.
body: Lachung's people, the Lachungpas, are Bhutia families who still govern the village through the Dzumsa, an elected council headed by a Pipon. A number of households now let rooms, and staying with one means eating thukpa, local greens and butter tea by the kitchen stove rather than a hotel buffet, and hearing first-hand about apple orchards, yak herds and the winter move down the valley.

Rooms are simple, usually with an attached or shared bathroom and plenty of quilts. We match guests to families we have stayed with, and tell you honestly which have hot running water. Homestays still need a registered agent for permits and vehicle. Check current status before you travel.
why: Meals cooked by a Lachungpa family, not a hotel kitchen
Half the price of most Lachung hotels
Close view of a village that runs itself through the Dzumsa

faqs.q: Are homestays allowed in Lachung for tourists?
faqs.a: Yes. Several Lachung families host guests, and some list on booking sites. You still need a protected area permit through a Sikkim Tourism-registered agent and a registered tourist vehicle, exactly as with a hotel. Local rules are set by the Dzumsa, the village council, and can change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What food do Lachung homestays serve?
faqs.a: Expect simple home cooking: rice, dal, seasonal vegetables, eggs or chicken, thukpa noodle soup, momos on request and butter or milk tea. Some families serve local greens and churpi (hard cheese). Vegetarian meals are easy. Tell us early about allergies, since the nearest large market is in Mangan, about two hours away.

faqs.q: Is a homestay warm enough in Lachung?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if you bring the right clothes. Families provide thick quilts, and the kitchen stove is the warmest room in the house. Few homestays have room heaters. From December to February we suggest thermals, a warm cap and socks for sleeping, or a comfort-tier hotel if anyone in your group struggles with cold.

name: Summit Gangchen
summary: Run by the Sikkim-based Summit Hotels group, Summit Gangchen is the largest and best-equipped hotel in Lachen, with electrically heated beds and a multi-cuisine restaurant. It is the comfort choice before the 4 am start for Gurudongmar Lake.
body: Lachen is a short night: you arrive in the late afternoon from Gangtok and leave around 4 to 5 am for Gurudongmar Lake. That makes a warm bed and an early breakfast worth paying for. Summit Gangchen, which the group describes as the largest hotel in Lachen, offers electrically heated beds, a restaurant and parking, and its staff are used to Gurudongmar timings.

Lachen reopened to tourists in stages in 2025–26 after long closures, and capacity is still limited, so book early. At about 2,750 m, Lachen is the night that prepares your body for 5,000 m the next morning: drink water, eat light and sleep early. Check current status before you travel.
why: Heated beds before the coldest morning of your trip
The best-equipped hotel in a small village
Staff used to packed breakfasts for Gurudongmar starts

faqs.q: Is Lachen open for tourists in 2026?
faqs.a: As we understand it, Lachen and Gurudongmar reopened on 9 March 2026, closed again in April after a landslide, and the road was repaired by 29 August 2026, with permits resuming around 11–12 September 2026. Openings depend on weather and road work, so check current status before you travel. We confirm every Lachen booking a few days before departure.

faqs.q: Why stay at a better hotel in Lachen?
faqs.a: Because you sleep only a few hours. Most Gurudongmar trips leave Lachen between 4 and 5 am, reach the lake at about 5,150–5,430 m around 8 to 9 am, and return to Lachen or drive on to Lachung. A heated bed and a reliable early breakfast help you rest and acclimatise, which reduces headaches at the lake.

faqs.q: Can foreigners stay at Summit Gangchen in Lachen?
faqs.a: The rules for foreign nationals in Lachen and Thangu are unclear at present, and foreigners are not allowed to Gurudongmar Lake. Foreigners can usually visit Lachung, Yumthang and Zero Point with a protected area permit through a registered agent, in a group of two or more. Ask us before you plan Lachen.

name: Lachen family homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,200–2,000 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Lachenpa families in the old village above the road host guests in wooden and stone houses, with dinner and an early breakfast. A low-cost, personal alternative to Lachen's package hotels, best for travellers who do not need room heaters.
body: Lachen, like Lachung, is governed by its own Dzumsa, the traditional council headed by an elected Pipon, and its people have close links with the Dokpa yak herders of the high pastures towards Thangu and beyond. A family homestay is the simplest way to hear about that life: the summer move of herds, the winter move down to lower villages, and how the 2023 and 2024 floods and slides changed the valley.

Rooms are basic but clean, with heavy quilts. Hosts are used to cooking breakfast at 3:30 am for Gurudongmar starts. Hot water may be by bucket. We place guests only with families we know, and a registered agent and vehicle are still required. Check current status before you travel.
why: Lowest-cost night in Lachen with home-cooked food
Hosts who know the Dzumsa and the high pastures first-hand
Early breakfasts for Gurudongmar are routine

faqs.q: Are there homestays in Lachen?
faqs.a: Yes. A number of Lachen families host guests, alongside the village's hotels. Lachen is small and opens and closes with the road, so availability is limited. You still need a protected area permit and a registered tourist vehicle arranged by a Sikkim Tourism-registered agent. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How cold is a Lachen homestay?
faqs.a: Lachen sits at about 2,750 m. In October–November nights fall close to 0 °C, and from December to February well below. Homestays usually have thick quilts but no room heater. Sleep in thermals and a cap, keep a water bottle inside your quilt so it does not freeze, and choose a hotel if anyone in your group is very sensitive to cold.

faqs.q: Can we see yaks from Lachen?
faqs.a: Usually yes, but higher up rather than in the village. Yaks graze around Thangu, Chopta Valley and the road to Gurudongmar, tended by Dokpa and Lachenpa herders, and you often pass herds on the drive. Ask before photographing herders or their camps, keep a distance from the animals, and never feed them.

name: Hotel Tamarind
summary: A Jain Group hotel on the North Sikkim Highway at Mangan, one of the few larger hotels in the district headquarters. Useful as a halfway night or a base for Dzongu and Singhik, with spacious rooms and views over Mangan, though upkeep is uneven.
body: Most travellers drive straight past Mangan, the Mangan district headquarters at about 956 m, on the way to Lachung or Lachen. Hotel Tamarind is the place we use when a later start, a landslide hold-up or a Dzongu day trip makes a night in Mangan sensible. It sits on the highway, rooms are large, and the upper floors look over the town and the Teesta gorge.

Reviews are mixed: staff are praised, but some guests say maintenance has slipped over the years. We ask for recently refreshed rooms. Mangan has banks, pharmacies and a market, which Lachung and Lachen lack. Check current status before you travel.
why: A practical halfway night on the North Sikkim Highway
Large rooms with views over Mangan and the Teesta gorge
Banks, pharmacies and the market close by

faqs.q: Should we stay a night in Mangan?
faqs.a: Only if it helps your plan. Most North Sikkim packages drive Gangtok to Lachung or Lachen in one day. A Mangan night makes sense if you start late from Bagdogra, want to visit Dzongu or Singhik, or a landslide delays you. Mangan is about 67 km and 2.5–3 hours from Gangtok.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to stay in Mangan?
faqs.a: No. Mangan town itself does not need a protected area permit for Indian travellers, and Indian visitors can stay there freely. Permits are needed beyond the Toong and Chungthang check posts for Lachung and Lachen, and to enter Dzongu. Foreign nationals need their Sikkim restricted area permit in any case. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is there to do near Hotel Tamarind?
faqs.a: Singhik viewpoint, about 4 km up the highway, faces Kangchenjunga and Siniolchu on clear mornings. Dzongu, the Lepcha reserve across the Teesta, is a half-day or overnight trip with a permit. Mangan is also the centre of Sikkim's large cardamom country, and you can walk the bazaar for local produce.

name: Mayal Lyang Homestay
price_band: ≈ ₹1,800–2,800 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: A Lepcha family homestay at Passingdang in Upper Dzongu, run by Gyatso Lepcha and his family, one of the first in Dzongu. Wooden rooms, farm food from the family's own fields, and walks, birding and river camping with village guides.
body: Mayal Lyang means hidden land in Lepcha, the name of the sacred homeland from which, in Lepcha belief, the people come and to which they return. The homestay sits on the slope at Passingdang above the Rongyong river, about 30 minutes from Mangan bazaar in good conditions. It is run by Gyatso Lepcha, one of the young Dzongu Lepchas who took part in the 2007–08 protests against hydropower projects in the reserve, and who then helped start homestay tourism as a local livelihood.

The house is built in the traditional way with wooden floors, and toilets sit outside the main house, as Lepcha custom keeps them apart from the home. Meals are cooked on a wood stove from Dzongu produce. Check current status before you travel.
why: One of Dzongu's founding homestays, run by a Lepcha family
Farm-to-plate meals cooked on the wood stove
Village walks, birding and river camping with local guides

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to stay at Mayal Lyang in Dzongu?
faqs.a: Yes. Dzongu is a reserved Lepcha area, and outsiders need a permit to enter. Indian travellers usually get it at Mangan with ID and photos, often with help from the homestay host. Foreign nationals face tighter rules: ask us before you plan. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does Mayal Lyang have attached bathrooms?
faqs.a: No. The house follows Lepcha tradition, in which toilets are not part of the home, so bathrooms sit a short walk away. They are kept clean, and hot water is provided. If an attached bathroom matters to you, tell us, and we will suggest another Dzongu homestay or a night in Mangan instead.

faqs.q: How many nights should we spend at Mayal Lyang?
faqs.a: Two nights is the minimum we suggest, three if you want to walk. One full day lets you hike to neighbouring villages, visit a cardamom field and sit by the Rongyong. A second day allows a river camp or a longer walk towards Lingthem or Lingzya. Dzongu is about slowing down, not ticking sights.

name: Dzongu Lepcha homestays
price_band: ≈ ₹1,500–2,500 per person a night with meals (indicative)
summary: Lepcha families across Dzongu villages such as Lingthem, Lingdong, Passingdang and Hee Gyathang host guests in traditional homes. Homestays began here around 2006–08 as a local alternative to large dams, and remain the only way to stay in the reserve.
body: Dzongu has no conventional hotels. Instead, Lepcha households in Upper and Lower Dzongu take guests, with meals of local rice, millet, nettle soup, greens and cardamom-country cooking. The homestay movement grew out of the 2007–08 protests by the Affected Citizens of Teesta against hydropower projects in the reserve, when young Lepchas looked for an income that kept the land and rivers intact.

Standards vary from simple farmhouse rooms to newer cottages with attached baths. We match travellers to families we know, according to comfort and walking ability. You need a Dzongu permit, and roads were damaged in the 2023 flood and the 2024 monsoon. Check current status before you travel.
why: The only way to stay inside the Lepcha reserve
Money goes directly to Lepcha families
Walks, birding and food you will not find on a package menu

faqs.q: Why are there no hotels in Dzongu?
faqs.a: Dzongu is a reserve for the Lepcha people, protected by a royal proclamation of the Chogyal era generally dated to 1956, under which outsiders cannot settle or buy land. Tourism has grown through family homestays rather than outside-owned hotels. That keeps visitor numbers small and the income local, but it also means simple rooms.

faqs.q: Which Dzongu village is best for a homestay?
faqs.a: It depends on what you want. Upper Dzongu villages such as Lingthem and Passingdang have Kangchenjunga views on clear days and are the road head for Tholung. Lower Dzongu villages such as Hee Gyathang are closer to Mangan. Tell us your walking ability and comfort needs and we will suggest a family.

faqs.q: Is Dzongu safe to visit after the floods?
faqs.a: Dzongu was hit by the October 2023 Teesta flood and by monsoon landslides in 2024, which damaged roads and bridges. Villages are inhabited and many homestays have reopened, but access can change after heavy rain. Avoid June to August, and check current status before you travel. We confirm road conditions with hosts before each booking.
